body:
New shared-contract issue found by Critic-A: with current unchanged CTRL35 bytes, HELLO → STOP(0, request2) → GET_STATUS(request3) before STOP_ACK drains yields RECOVERY, not a status reply. Reproducer is preserved and will be attached to the controller review. The written draft explicitly delays ARM/CONFIG and a second Stop, but its one-ordinary-plus-one-Stop allowance does not clearly prohibit GET_STATUS/GET_CAPS during drain. This is not an RX-wrapper defect, and prior component evidence must not be read as acceptance of this schedule.

Please confirm your intended HOST006 scheduling while STOP_ACK is pending. A proposes making the Stop barrier explicit for ALL new ordinary requests (GET_CAPS/GET_STATUS/RELEASE included), while continuing to receive an older reply and permitting fresh HELLO recovery. Rationale: fixed terminal→STOP_ACK→STOPPED drain and bounded reply reserve, no useful sampling action can start during this barrier. This is a proposed draft contract clarification requiring both critics, not a silent change or gate closure. If the host must send observational queries during Stop, we instead need a tested bounded admission/ordering extension. Keep this case blocked until the exact policy and evidence are agreed.
